extracted.intended_audience: general readers, anime/manga fans, and researchers interested in media controversies
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic (Wikipedia) overview of the manga/anime series Kodomo no Jikan covering publication, characters, adaptations, music, and the criticism/controversy surrounding its sexual content involving minors and resulting censorship/publishing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness for North American audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven Seas Entertainment delayed and ultimately cancelled its English release citing concerns about the relationship between an elementary school student and her adult teacher and that 'later volumes in the series can not be considered appropriate for the US market by any reasonable standard.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher reasoning included vendor/retailer objections and re-review of later anthologies that revealed scenes considered highly unsuitable for publication in North America (examples cited: intimate relationships between cousins; a bath scene with a child and adult; a scene where a child rubs her crotch against the adult teacher).

rubrics_metrics.name: Television broadcast suitability and reasons for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Japanese TV stations (e.g., TV Saitama and Mie TV) removed the anime from their broadcast schedules; TV Saitama stated its decision was heavily influenced by the then-recent capture of a notorious Japanese child pornographer who was revealed to be an elementary school vice principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasters considered the social context and potential association with real-world scandals when deciding to pull the show, indicating sensitivity to public perception and legal/ethical implications beyond the content itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship level by medium (broadcast vs DVD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content of the broadcast version was sometimes heavily censored, while the DVD releases of the individual episodes remain unedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censorship ranged from animated panels obscuring parts of the screen and sound effects used to 'bleep' dialogue, to full suppression of both audio and video; uncensored versions were available on DVD and in OVAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of sexual content involving minors (classification as 'lolicon' or obscene)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics labeled the content 'lolicon' or 'comic book kiddie porn', expressing complete disapproval of the sexualized depiction of minors and the central student–teacher relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical classification influenced public discourse and publisher decisions; specific scenes cited by critics (e.g., forced sexual advances, rubbing against an adult) were used as evidence for these classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher licensing and market/retailer considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing and publishing decisions were influenced by vendors and retailers dropping orders and the perceived market acceptability of the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seven Seas cited vendors 'dropping their orders left and right' as a factor leading to cancellation; conversely, Digital Manga later licensed the series and attempted a Kickstarter to fund English print editions, showing that commercial and community funding considerations can override/supplement traditional retail channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and legal boundary crossings by characters as evaluative factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The manga's characters are described as crossing 'moral and legal boundaries' many times (e.g., a student making sexual advances on a teacher, threatening to accuse him of molestation), which forms part of why the work is controversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of character behavior are used to assess whether the work violates commonly accepted moral/legal norms and therefore whether it is suitable for certain audiences or distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural differences in reception and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Creator Kaworu Watashiya commented that reactions to the content highlighted 'differences in the cultures between the countries,' implying varying thresholds for acceptability across markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural context may alter how particular content (e.g., sexualized minors, cousin relationships) is perceived and whether it is licensed, broadcast, or censored in different countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketability and publisher financial viability affecting release
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-licensing publication efforts (e.g., Digital Manga's Kickstarter to publish omnibus volumes) succeeded in fundraising, but later financial difficulties at the publisher caused delays in fulfillment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when content is deemed legally/politically acceptable for release, publisher financial health, fulfillment capability, and logistics can be decisive for whether and how a work reaches readers (e-book vs print, Kickstarter vs retail).
